issues.description: The problem text explicitly instructs students to use StringBuilder for the Animal name attribute, but the provided solution (and its Animal.java) defines the name attribute as a String. This is a cross-artifact attribute type mismatch that can confuse students about the required type and how to implement constructors/getters/setters and subclasses.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and the reference implementation consistent. Either (A) update the reference solution and template to use a StringBuilder field for the Animal name (change the attribute type, adjust constructor to accept a String or StringBuilder and initialize the StringBuilder, and update getters/setters accordingly), or (B) relax the problem text to require a String name (remove the StringBuilder instruction). Preferably keep the problem text and change the code to use StringBuilder so students practice the intended type.

issues.description: Within the problem statement itself there is a contradiction: the UML diagram shows the Animal name attribute type as String, while the textual instruction later requires using StringBuilder for the name attribute. This inner-artifact inconsistency can confuse students about the expected attribute type.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: either update the UML to show name: StringBuilder to match the textual instruction, or change the textual instruction to require String. Ensure the specification consistently communicates the expected attribute type so students implement the correct design.
